answer.rationale: Renewal is the only near-term lever that can pursue the mandated cut without forcing a primary-vendor change while the line is at 94% with no buffer and 14 days to expiry. I want to verify memory_c4 because it is the strongest evidence that benchmarking at renewal can move an incumbent despite an initial refusal; if accurate, I would open a narrow renewal renegotiation focused on benchmarked price/payment/volume terms rather than switch supply. Switching primary is attractive for cost but too risky this cycle; deferral is unavailable because the contract does not auto-renew; adding a second source helps resilience but is unlikely to deliver the immediate 18% cut within capacity.
